environment: RTX 2050 (4 GB) · deepseek-coder-1.3b-base NF4 · seed 0 · 3 identical repeats
round_shape: 6 client uploads → 4 aggregations → 4 registry versions → 4 composites → 2 decisions
note: The primary metric the D5 promotion rule reads. For each client a deterministic slice of its files is held out and never trained on; next-line completion is run over 60 held-out examples with greedy decoding and scored as edit similarity (character-level 1 - lev/max_len, CodeXGLUE convention) and exact match. Perplexity is the third field and comes from P1's held-out training eval. HumanEval/MBPP pass@k is the separate regression guard (see the Pass@k page) and is currently unscored on this OS.

aggregation_ablation.caption: Relative Frobenius error of the aggregate vs. the exact FedProx-weighted average (lower is better).

in_project_completion.caption: In-project next-line completion — 60 held-out examples, greedy.

takeaway: The SVD aggregate beats the naive ablation on the metric the promotion rule actually reads, in both clusters — the mathematically correct aggregation produces a measurably better model on the completion task, not just a smaller norm error.
